messages:
Nina: Heads up — seeing a big spillback of small GPU jobs from us-west1-a into b/c. Lots of preemptions and a surge in evictions starting ~09:10 UTC.
Alex: Yep noticed that. Dashboard shows node-util on spot pools dropping to 10% while dedicated pools are full.
Nina: Eviction noise looks like a mix of taints + pod anti-affinity failures. Some pods are tiny (0.25 GPU) and get scattered across AZs.
Alex: paste:
```
Events:
  Warning  Evicted    3s (x12 over 2m)  kubelet  The node had condition: DiskPressure
  Normal   Preempted  1s (x8 over 2m)   kube-scheduler  Preempting low-priority pods
```
Sam: @Nina can you share a couple pod specs? curious about tolerations/affinity.
Nina: sending one example:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: train-small-xyz
spec:
  containers:
  - name: runner
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25"
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: []
  tolerations: []
```
Maria: Oof 0.25 GPU is rough for binpack. Scheduler ends up spreading them which increases cross-AZ traffic and fills many nodes with tiny leftovers. :thinking:
Jonathan: We probably need a mixed strategy: enforce soft podAffinity for same-node for these "micro-gpu" jobs + a descheduler footgun that squashes leftovers into consolidation cycles.
Sam: Also saw autoscaler scale-down aggressively in us-west1-b at the same time — scale-down is evicting and then scale-up doesn't reclaim same node types, causing fragmentation. Disabling scale-down helped in testing.
Nina: Short-term mitigation applied: bumped binpack threshold for spot pools to 0.5 GPU, disabled aggressive scale-down for 15m, and labeled large-batch nodes with "gpu.compaction=true" for placement targeting.
devops-bot: Incident alert: evictions > 50/min in eng-gpu-spot-us-west1 between 09:08-09:22 UTC. Pager: on-call Sam.
Sam: I'll run a targeted descheduler job (consolidate and prefer same-node) and push a scheduler predicate tweak to prefer co-locating sub-gpu pods. Will monitor cost impact.
Maria: Long-term: propose a "micro-gpu" class nodepool with tighter packing + local ephemeral storage SLO so we avoid DiskPressure churn. Also consider group-aware preemption to avoid bursty eviction waves.
Jonathan: Agree. Also let's add a cheap admission controller that rejects 0.25 GPU requests unless they opt into a micro-gpu nodepool label. That will reduce scatter.
Nina: Thanks all — will keep the mitigations running and post metrics in 30m. If anyone sees a resume of evictions tag @sam. :thumbsup:
Alex: Nice work. Also capturing cost delta after packing — initial sim shows ~18% lower GPU-hours when micro-gpu binpack works.
Maria: Recording action items: 1) Sam run descheduler + scheduler tweak 2) Nina keep mitigations 3) Jonathan design admission controller 4) Product: evaluate dev impact on latency for small jobs.
Nina: cc @all — adding notes to runbook after this calms down.
